title: क्या भीषण गर्मी के कई दिनों के बाद उत्तर में एक बार फिर भारी बारिश होने वाली है? - Vietnam.vn

क्या भीषण गर्मी के कई दिनों के बाद उत्तर में एक बार फिर भारी बारिश होने वाली है?
मौसम पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, लगभग 17 या 18 अगस्त से उत्तरी क्षेत्र में हल्की बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश होगी (बारिश दोपहर और शाम के समय केंद्रित रहेगी)।
Báo Gia đình và Xã hội•12/08/2026
उत्तरी वियतनाम में इन गर्म दिनों के बाद कब भारी बारिश होगी जिससे गर्मी कम हो सके?
वीटीवी के मौसम पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, हनोई , उत्तरी वियतनाम और उत्तर मध्य वियतनाम में गर्म मौसम जारी है। इसका कारण क्षेत्र में उत्तर से उत्तर-पश्चिम की ओर चलने वाली तेज़ हवाओं का निरंतर प्रभाव है।
आज उत्तरी वियतनाम के सभी वार्डों में, जिनमें होआन किएम वार्ड (हनोई) भी शामिल है, तापमान आमतौर पर 36-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहेगा।
राष्ट्रीय जल-मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र के 10 दिवसीय मौसम पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, उत्तरी क्षेत्र में लू की लहर सप्ताह के अंत तक जारी रहेगी। आज रात से बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान बढ़ने की संभावना है।
लगभग 17 या 18 अगस्त से, हल्की बारिश और छिटपुट गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, जिनमें कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है (बारिश दोपहर और शाम के समय अधिक होगी)। गरज के साथ बौछारों के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओले पड़ने और तेज हवा के झोंके चलने की संभावना है।
मध्य क्षेत्र में, थान्ह होआ से लेकर खान्ह होआ तक आज का मौसम भीषण गर्मी से भरा है, तापमान 37-38 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया है। इस लू के कई और दिनों तक जारी रहने का अनुमान है।
मध्य पर्वतीय और दक्षिणी क्षेत्रों में सुबह से दोपहर तक धूप खिली रहेगी। मध्य पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में तापमान 29-33 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा; जबकि दक्षिण में तापमान 32-34 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक रहेगा।
मौसम पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, मध्य उच्चभूमि और वियतनाम के दक्षिणपूर्वी क्षेत्र में दोपहर बाद से छिटपुट गरज के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना है, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है। गरज के साथ बारिश के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने और तेज हवाओं का खतरा हो सकता है, इसलिए सावधानी बरतने की सलाह दी जाती है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
देश के सभी क्षेत्रों के लिए 10 दिनों का मौसम पूर्वानुमान।
13 अगस्त की रात से 14 अगस्त की सुबह तक का मौसम पूर्वानुमान:
- उत्तरी वियतनाम: शाम और रात में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में धूप और गर्मी रहेगी, हालांकि लाई चाऊ, डिएन बिएन , सोन ला, क्वांग निन्ह और हाई फोंग के कुछ इलाकों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ सकती है।
- थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर, पूर्वी क्वांग न्गाई से डैक लक और खान्ह होआ तक के क्षेत्र: शाम और रात में कुछ क्षेत्रों में बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान; दिन के दौरान धूप और गर्मी रहेगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ेगा।
- मध्य हाइलैंड्स और दक्षिणी वियतनाम: दोपहर बाद और शाम को छिटपुट बौछारें और गरज के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना है (बारिश मध्य हाइलैंड्स और पूर्वी दक्षिणी वियतनाम में केंद्रित होगी), कुछ क्षेत्रों में छिटपुट बौछारें और गरज के साथ बारिश होगी, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है, खासकर 14 अगस्त की शाम को; दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी।
- अन्य क्षेत्र: दोपहर और शाम के बाद कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में धूप रहेगी, हालांकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में गर्मी रहेगी।
तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओले गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना रहती है।
14 अगस्त की रात से 22 अगस्त तक का मौसम पूर्वानुमान:
- उत्तरी वियतनाम: शाम और रात में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी; दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी, कुछ इलाकों में गर्मी रहेगी। लगभग 17 या 18 अगस्त से छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी, कुछ इलाकों में भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है (बारिश शाम और रात में केंद्रित रहेगी)।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर और क्वांग न्गाई प्रांत के पूर्वी भाग से लेकर डाक लक तक का क्षेत्र: शाम और रात में कुछ क्षेत्रों में बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में धूप और गर्मी रहेगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ेगा। 15 अगस्त से मध्य क्षेत्र में लू धीरे-धीरे कम होने लगेगी।
- मध्य और दक्षिणी हाइलैंड्स: कुछ क्षेत्रों में बौछारें और गरज के साथ बारिश होगी, खासकर दोपहर और शाम के समय छिटपुट बौछारें और गरज के साथ बारिश होगी, और कुछ स्थानों पर स्थानीय रूप से भारी बारिश हो सकती है।
- अन्य क्षेत्र: दोपहर और शाम के बाद कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में धूप रहेगी, हालांकि कुछ क्षेत्रों में गर्मी रहेगी।
तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओले गिरने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना रहती है।

title: यूरोप की आधी से अधिक आबादी को एक नई भीषण गर्मी की लहर का सामना करना पड़ रहा है। - Vietnam.vn

full_text:
यूरोप की आधी से अधिक आबादी को 12 अगस्त को 30 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर के तापमान का सामना करना पड़ा, जिसमें लगभग 92 मिलियन लोगों ने 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर के तापमान का अनुभव किया, क्योंकि एक नई लू ने महाद्वीप के कई हिस्सों को अपनी चपेट में ले रखा था।
पश्चिमी और दक्षिणी यूरोप के सबसे बुरी तरह प्रभावित होने की आशंका है, जिनमें फ्रांस, इटली और स्पेन सबसे अधिक प्रभावित देशों में शामिल हैं।
स्पेन में देश के अधिकांश हिस्सों में भीषण गर्मी की चेतावनी जारी की गई है, जिसमें उत्तर-पश्चिम से दक्षिण-पूर्व तक तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक रहने की आशंका है।
फ्रांस के कई क्षेत्रों में भी इसी तरह का तापमान दर्ज किया गया, जबकि उत्तर-पूर्वी और पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में मौसम अधिक सुहावना था।
लू का प्रकोप बाल्कन क्षेत्र, विशेषकर ग्रीस और एड्रियाटिक तट तक भी फैल गया है। लंबे समय तक उच्च तापमान के कारण सूखा और भी गंभीर हो रहा है, ऊर्जा प्रणालियों पर दबाव बढ़ रहा है, फसलों पर असर पड़ रहा है और जंगल में आग लगने का खतरा बढ़ रहा है।
पेरिस में वियतनाम न्यूज एजेंसी के संवाददाता के अनुसार, 12 अगस्त को फ्रांस में परमाणु ऊर्जा उत्पादन क्षमता का लगभग 20% हिस्सा बाधित हो गया था।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
ले मोंडे के अनुसार, यह स्थिति सूखे, अत्यधिक गर्मी और जेलीफिश के प्रकोप से संबंधित है जो रिएक्टर को ठंडा करने के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले पंपों को अवरुद्ध कर देती है।
विशेषज्ञों का मानना है कि अत्यधिक मछली पकड़ना, प्लास्टिक प्रदूषण और जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण समुद्र के पानी का गर्म होना जेलीफिश के पनपने के लिए अनुकूल परिस्थितियां पैदा कर रहे हैं।
ब्रिटेन में, स्कॉटलैंड सहित कई क्षेत्रों में जंगल की आग की चेतावनी अभी भी प्रभावी है।
ब्रिटेन के मौसम विभाग का अनुमान है कि कई इलाकों में तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक हो सकता है, और मध्य, पूर्वी और दक्षिण-पूर्वी क्षेत्रों में यह 36-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच सकता है। ब्रिटिश सरकार भीषण गर्मी से निपटने के लिए इस साल की अपनी दूसरी कोबरा आपातकालीन बैठक बुलाने की तैयारी कर रही है।
देश की मौसम विज्ञान एजेंसी का अनुमान है कि ब्रिटेन अब तक की सबसे गर्म गर्मी की ओर बढ़ रहा है।
वैज्ञानिकों के अनुसार, जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण यूरोप में भीषण गर्मी, शुष्क मौसम और जंगल की आग जैसी चरम मौसमी घटनाओं की आवृत्ति बढ़ रही है। यूरोप वर्तमान में दुनिया का सबसे तेजी से गर्म होने वाला महाद्वीप है, और इस गर्मी में भी कई क्षेत्रों में लगातार लू, भीषण सूखा और जंगल की आग का प्रकोप जारी है।

राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान और जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, उत्तरी क्षेत्र (लाई चाऊ और डिएन बिएन को छोड़कर), थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक, प्रांतों के पूर्वी हिस्से क्वांग न्गाई से डाक लक और खान्ह होआ तक, लू और भीषण गर्मी का सामना कर रहे हैं।
आज (13 अगस्त): उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी जारी है, लाओ काई के कुछ इलाकों में तापमान 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया है।
13 अगस्त, 2026 के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान: उत्तरी वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी जारी रहेगी और कुछ क्षेत्रों में तापमान 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक रहेगा; मध्य वियतनाम लू की चपेट में रहेगा।
मौसम पूर्वानुमानों के अनुसार, 13 अगस्त को उत्तरी वियतनाम में गर्म मौसम जारी रहेगा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ेगी। लाई चाऊ और डिएन बिएन में धूप खिली रहेगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में गर्म मौसम रहेगा और अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा, जबकि कुछ स्थानों पर यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी हो सकता है; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 55-60% रहेगी; दोपहर और शाम के बाद छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है।
लाओ काई प्रांत में, टाइफून डॉल्फिन से कमजोर हुए निम्न दबाव क्षेत्र के सुदूर दक्षिण-पश्चिमी किनारे के प्रभाव और ऊपरी स्तर पर अपसरण क्षेत्र के कारण, 13 और 14 अगस्त को प्रांत के निचले इलाकों में भीषण गर्मी जारी रही। अधिकतम तापमान 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुँच गया; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता 50-55% थी।
14 अगस्त को उत्तरी क्षेत्र (डिएन बिएन, लाई चाऊ, सोन ला, क्वांग निन्ह और हाई फोंग को छोड़कर) में गर्म मौसम जारी रहा, हालांकि इसकी तीव्रता पहले से कम थी। अधिकतम तापमान 35-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में यह 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक था; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 60-65% थी।
पूर्वानुमानों से संकेत मिलता है कि 15 अगस्त से उत्तरी क्षेत्र में व्यापक लू की लहर समाप्त होने की संभावना है और मध्य क्षेत्र में यह कम होने लगेगी।
मौसम विज्ञान एजेंसी सलाह देती है कि लू के दौरान, लोगों को दोपहर और दोपहर बाद के शुरुआती समय के बीच (जब गर्मी सबसे तीव्र होती है) बाहरी गतिविधियों को कम से कम करना चाहिए।
विशेष रूप से, सतह की स्थितियों (कंक्रीट, डामर) और आर्द्रता के आधार पर, वास्तविक रूप से महसूस किया गया बाहरी तापमान पूर्वानुमानित तापमान से 1-3 डिग्री अधिक हो सकता है।

सावन में भी बारिश को तरसे लोग, छाए रहेंगे बादल पर धूप और उमस से छूटेगे पसीने

सावन के महीने में भी पूर्णिया और सीमांचल के लोग बारिश के लिए तरस रहे हैं. आसमान में बादल छाए रहने के बावजूद तीखी धूप और उमस से लोग बेहाल हैं, तापमान 35 डिग्री तक पहुंचने का अनुमान है. मौसम विभाग हल्की बारिश के आसार जता रहा है, लेकिन फिलहाल राहत मुश्किल दिख रही है.
सावन के महीने में जहां झमाझम बारिश की उम्मीद रहती है, वहीं पूर्णिया और पूरे सीमांचल के लोगों को मौसम से लगातार निराशा ही हाथ लग रही है. आसमान में बादलों की आवाजाही के बावजूद लोग बारिश की एक-एक बूंद के लिए तरस रहे हैं. मंगलवार की सुबह भले ही सुहावनी रही, लेकिन दिन चढ़ने के साथ ही तीखी धूप, भारी उमस और चिपचिपी गर्मी लोगों को बेहाल करने वाली है.
मौसम विभाग ने नहीं जारी की चेतावनी, पर बारिश के आसार
मौसम विभाग (IMD) की ओर से आज पूर्णिया जिले के लिए किसी तरह की अलर्ट या चेतावनी जारी नहीं की गई है. मौसम पूर्वानुमान इंडेक्स के अनुसार, आसमान में आंशिक रूप से बादल छाए रहने और एक-दो स्थानों पर हल्की से मध्यम बारिश होने की गुंजाइश जरूर बनी हुई है. हालांकि, बादलों के बीच धूप खिलने से दिनभर उमस का असर काफी अधिक देखने को मिलेगा.
35 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंचेगा पारा
पूर्णिया के तापमान की बात करें तो आज जिले का अधिकतम तापमान 35.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 28.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने का अनुमान है. कमजोर मानसून और तीखी धूप के कारण तापमान सामान्य से अधिक महसूस होगा. स्थानीय लोगों का कहना है कि बादलों की मौजूदगी के बाद भी बारिश न होने से उमस की स्थिति और अधिक गंभीर हो गई है.
तेज हवाओं के साथ छिटपुट बारिश की संभावना
आइएमडी के सामान्य पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, दिन के उत्तरार्ध में जिले में तेज हवाओं के साथ कुछ इलाकों में छिटपुट बौछारें पड़ सकती हैं. किसानों और आम लोगों को उम्मीद है कि यदि हवाओं की दिशा अनुकूल रही, तो मानसून का यह मिजाज बदलेगा और आने वाले दिनों में अच्छी बारिश से राहत मिल सकेगी.

title: हरियाणा में आज रात से मानसून फिर पकड़ेगा रफ्तार, 15 अगस्त तक तेज बारिश का अलर्ट - ETV Bharat

full_text:
हरियाणा में आज रात से मानसून फिर पकड़ेगा रफ्तार, 15 अगस्त तक तेज बारिश का अलर्ट
हरियाणा में आज रात से मानसून सक्रिय होगा. 15 अगस्त तक गरज-चमक, तेज हवा के साथ तेज बारिश के आसार हैं.
चंडीगढ़: हरियाणा में पिछले दिनों सुस्त पड़ा मानसून अब एक बार फिर सक्रिय होने जा रहा है. मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक आज रात से प्रदेश में मानसूनी गतिविधियां बढ़ने की संभावना है. 15 अगस्त तक ज्यादातर हिस्सों में गरज-चमक और तेज हवाओं के साथ बारिश हो सकती है.
मानसून टर्फ उत्तर की ओर खिसकने के आसार: मौसम वैज्ञानिक डॉ. मदन खीचड़ ने बताया कि, "आज मानसून टर्फ की अक्षय रेखा के उत्तर की तरफ खिसकने और राजस्थान के ऊपर चक्रवातीय परिसंचरण बनने से हरियाणा में मानसूनी गतिविधियां बढ़ेंगी. इसके प्रभाव से कई इलाकों में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश होने की संभावना है, जबकि कुछ स्थानों पर तेज बारिश भी हो सकती है."
15 अगस्त तक बारिश का दौर: मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक आज रात से 15 अगस्त के दौरान प्रदेश के अधिकांश हिस्सों में बादल छाए रहेंगे. इस दौरान हवाओं के साथ गरज-चमक देखने को मिल सकती है. कुछ स्थानों पर तेज बारिश होने का अनुमान है. बादल छाए रहने के कारण दिन के तापमान में मामूली गिरावट आएगी, जबकि रात के तापमान में हल्की बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है.
4.2 डिग्री बढ़ा औसत अधिकतम तापमान: बीते 24 घंटों में हरियाणा के औसत अधिकतम तापमान में 4.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस की बढ़ोतरी दर्ज की गई. मौसम केंद्र चंडीगढ़ के अनुसार गुरुग्राम स्थित नॉर्थकैप यूनिवर्सिटी AWS में प्रदेश का सबसे अधिक तापमान 37.1°C रहा. चंडीगढ़ में 36.4°C, अंबाला में 36.2°C, हिसार और रोहतक में 35.4°C तथा करनाल में 34.5°C तापमान दर्ज किया गया.
गुरुग्राम में रात सबसे ठंडी: दिन में जहां गुरुग्राम सबसे गर्म रहा, वहीं रात के तापमान में प्रदेश में मामूली गिरावट दर्ज हुई. औसत न्यूनतम तापमान में 0.1°C की कमी आई. गुरुग्राम में न्यूनतम तापमान 22.0°C रहा, जो सामान्य से 4.3°C कम है. चंडीगढ़ में 24.4°C, पंचकूला में 24.8°C, भिवानी में 25°C और करनाल में 25.3°C तापमान दर्ज किया गया.
बारिश से तापमान में आएगी राहत: मौसम विभाग के अनुसार अगले कुछ दिनों में बादल और बारिश का असर दिन के तापमान पर दिखाई देगा. तेज धूप से बढ़े पारे में गिरावट आने की संभावना है. वहीं, बादलों की मौजूदगी के कारण रात का तापमान थोड़ा बढ़ सकता है. किसानों और आम लोगों को मौसम में बदलाव के दौरान सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी गई है.

एसकेडीएस - 12 अगस्त को दर्ज किए गए उच्चतम तापमान के अनुसार, उत्तरी आयरलैंड के कई इलाकों में तापमान 37-38 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जिसमें हनोई में 38.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक तापमान पहुंच गया।
Báo Sức khỏe và Đời sống•13/08/2026
सबसे अधिक तापमान वाले क्षेत्र
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, 12 अगस्त को उत्तरी क्षेत्र (लाई चाऊ और डिएन बिएन को छोड़कर), थान्ह होआ से दा नांग शहर तक, और प्रांतों के पूर्वी भाग, क्वांग न्गाई से डाक लक और खान्ह होआ तक, में भीषण गर्मी रहेगी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-38 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी हो सकता है, जैसे कि लाक सोन (फू थो) में 38.3 डिग्री, लैंग ( हनोई ) में 38.8 डिग्री, न्हो क्वान (निन्ह बिन्ह) में 38.5 डिग्री, तिन्ह जिया (थान्ह होआ) में 38.3 डिग्री, होआई न्होन (जिया लाई) में 38.8 डिग्री, आदि; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 50-60% रहेगी।
12 अगस्त को दर्ज किए गए उच्चतम तापमान के अनुसार, उत्तरी वियतनाम के कई इलाकों में तापमान 37-38 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहा। विशेष रूप से, लाक सोन (फू थो) में 38.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस; होआ बिन्ह में 38.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस; बाक मे (तुयेन क्वांग) में 38.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस; थाट खे (लैंग सोन) में 38.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस; और हाई डुओंग ( हाई फोंग ) में 38.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान दर्ज किया गया।
हनोई में, सबसे अधिक तापमान लैंग स्टेशन पर 38.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। हा डोंग स्टेशन पर 38.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस, सोन ताई में 37.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस और होआई डुक में 37.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान रहा।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
निन्ह बिन्ह क्षेत्र में भी उच्च तापमान दर्ज किया गया, जहां न्हो क्वान में 38.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान रहा। थान्ह होआ में, सबसे अधिक तापमान तिन्ह जिया में 38.3 डिग्री सेल्सियस, सैम सोन में 38.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस और थान्ह होआ में 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया।
न्घे आन प्रांत में, क्विन्ह लू में तापमान 38.1 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। हा तिन्ह प्रांत में, होन्ह सोन स्टेशन पर उच्चतम तापमान 37.7 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा।
ह्यू से दक्षिण की ओर भी तापमान अधिक रहा। ह्यू में 37.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस, दा नांग में 37.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस और क्वांग न्गाई में 37.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान दर्ज किया गया। विशेष रूप से, होआई न्होन (गिया लाई) में 38.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस, फान रंग (खान्ह होआ) में 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस और कैम रान्ह में 37.9 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान दर्ज किया गया।
आंकड़ों से पता चलता है कि 12 अगस्त को भीषण गर्मी की लहर व्यापक थी, कई मौसम केंद्रों ने 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक तापमान दर्ज किया। सबसे अधिक तापमान 38.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस लैंग (हनोई) और होआई न्होन ( जिया लाई ) में दर्ज किया गया।
मध्य वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी जारी है और तापमान 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक है।
13 अगस्त को उत्तरी क्षेत्र (डिएन बिएन, लाई चाऊ और क्वांग निन्ह को छोड़कर) में गर्म मौसम रहा, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस था, कुछ स्थानों पर यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी रहा; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 55-60% थी। 14 अगस्त को उत्तरी क्षेत्र (डिएन बिएन, लाई चाऊ, सोन ला, क्वांग निन्ह और हाई फोंग को छोड़कर) में गर्म मौसम रहा, अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस था, कुछ स्थानों पर यह 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी रहा; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 60-65% थी।
13-14 अगस्त को थान्ह होआ से ह्यू शहर तक के क्षेत्र में गर्म मौसम रहेगा, कुछ इलाकों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ेगी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 35-37 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा, कुछ स्थानों पर यह 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक भी हो सकता है; न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 55-60% रहेगी।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
दा नांग शहर, क्वांग न्गाई के पूर्वी भाग से लेकर डैक लक और खान्ह होआ तक के क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ेगी। अधिकतम तापमान आमतौर पर 36-38 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रहेगा और कुछ क्षेत्रों में 38 डिग्री सेल्सियस से भी अधिक हो सकता है। न्यूनतम सापेक्ष आर्द्रता आमतौर पर 50-55% रहेगी। 15 अगस्त से उत्तरी क्षेत्र में व्यापक लू समाप्त होने की संभावना है और मध्य क्षेत्र में इसका प्रभाव कम हो जाएगा। लू के कारण प्राकृतिक आपदा जोखिम चेतावनी स्तर 1 है।
भीषण गर्मी और कम आर्द्रता के कारण आवासीय क्षेत्रों में बिजली की मांग बढ़ने से विस्फोट और आग लगने का खतरा बढ़ जाता है। इसके अलावा, लंबे समय तक उच्च तापमान में रहने वाले लोगों में निर्जलीकरण भी हो सकता है।
कृपया ध्यान दें कि लू की रिपोर्टों में तापमान का पूर्वानुमान और बाहर का वास्तविक तापमान कंक्रीट या डामर जैसी सतहों की स्थिति के आधार पर 1-3 डिग्री या उससे भी अधिक भिन्न हो सकता है।

A rare amber weather warning for extreme heat is in effect across a large swathe of the UK on Thursday, with temperatures set to soar as high as 38C (100F).
Thursday will mark the peak of the UK's fifth widespread heatwave this year, with temperatures to be in the mid-30s Celsius across most of the warning area.
Amber heat health alerts, external, which warn of significant impacts to health and social care services, are also in force for the entirety of England until 21:00 BST on Friday.
The searing heat could lead to power cuts, rail and air travel delays, and cause serious health impacts such as dehydration and heat exhaustion.
The extreme heat warning will be in force until 23:59 BST across Eastern England, London and the south-east, the Midlands, north-west England, south-west England and parts of Yorkshire and Humber.
It will run alongside amber heat health alerts issued by the UK Health Security Agency across the entirety of England.
In effect until 21:00 BST on 14 August, these warn of significant impacts across health and social care services, including a rise in deaths, particularly among those aged 65 and over or with health conditions.
Adding to the risks associated with the heatwave, a few tropical nights - where temperatures fail to drop below 20C - are also on the cards as increasingly humid air spreads into western areas.
The cumulative effect of persistent heat by day and night can place additional stress on the body.
Fortunately, this heatwave is likely to be short-lived, lasting three days at most.
Temperatures will begin to fall away by the weekend, although at their lowest they will still be average or a little above average for mid-August.
More temperature records likely to fall
There are likely to be long-standing temperature records broken over the coming days, adding to a long list of records already set this year.
Wednesday became the first day in August to reach 35C or more, making it the 4th consecutive month to reach this temperature.
If temperatures reach 36C or higher, 2026 will become the first year on record to register four separate days at or above that threshold.
This will surpass the previous record of three days, which is currently shared by 1990, 2003, 2020 and 2026.
It is not out of the question that a few locations, including London, could touch 38C.
Should this happen, it would be the second time the UK hit 38C this summer - the highest reading so far this year - tied with Lingwood in Norfolk on 26 June.
Currently the hottest August day on record stands at 38.5C, recorded in 2003.
As long as August temperatures remain average or above for the month as a whole, this summer will replace 2025 as the warmest on record.

Japanese vending machine maker SDRS has developed a human-sized stainless-steel cooling booth to help people escape extreme heat.
The Do Hiemon Box can blow air as cold as 5°C and is designed to cool one person in about 20 minutes.
The invention comes as Japan experiences increasingly severe heatwaves and record numbers of heatstroke cases.
As Japan grapples with increasingly severe summer heat, a vending machine manufacturer has developed an unusual solution: a human-sized stainless-steel refrigerator designed to cool one person at a time and help prevent heatstroke.
Japanese manufacturer SDRS's Do Hiemon Box functions as a personal cooling booth, blowing air as cold as 5°C through vents at the top and rear. The product is being marketed as a quick way for people working or spending time outdoors to escape extreme temperatures.
How Does The 'Human Refrigerator' Work?
The Do Hiemon Box is an insulated stainless-steel enclosure measuring 1.75 metres (5.7 feet) in height and designed to accommodate a single person on a narrow seat.
Users can adjust the temperature and airflow through three settings, while cool air is circulated through vents positioned at the top and back of the booth.
The unit is mounted on casters and runs from a regular electrical outlet, allowing it to be moved between locations. Its developers envisage it being used at construction sites, factories and outdoor events where workers and visitors may need temporary relief from extreme heat.
Trusco Nakayama, which sells the product, claims that the booth can help cool the entire body in about 20 minutes while consuming roughly half the energy of an average portable air conditioner.
The company describes the concept as a "human refrigerator" and says it offers full-body cooling compared with wearable solutions such as fan-equipped jackets, which are commonly used by outdoor workers in Japan.
Why Is Japan Turning To Extreme Cooling Solutions?
The development comes as Japan experiences increasingly intense summer temperatures and a growing number of heat-related illnesses.
Japan recorded a particularly severe heatwave last year, while meteorologists have adopted the term "kokushobi", meaning "cruel heat day", for days when temperatures reach 40°C or higher.
Recently, Japan experienced an unprecedented five consecutive days of kokushobi conditions. In Tokyo alone, 453 people were reportedly hospitalised for heat-related illness in a single day — the highest figure recorded since monitoring began more than a decade ago. At least 14 people died across the country during the heatwave.
The extreme conditions have increased demand for ways to protect people who cannot simply remain indoors in air-conditioned spaces.
The Do Hiemon Box is particularly aimed at workers and others who spend long periods outside, offering a dedicated space where they can temporarily escape the heat.
Can 'Human Refrigerators' Solve The Heat Problem?
The cooling booth reflects a broader challenge facing countries experiencing more frequent and intense heatwaves: many solutions designed to protect people from heat also consume significant amounts of energy.
Air conditioning remains one of the most common ways of coping with extreme temperatures, but it contributes to the problem in several ways. Air-conditioning systems release waste heat into their surroundings and consume electricity, while refrigerants can contribute to warming when they leak.
The Do Hiemon Box is being promoted partly on its lower energy consumption compared with portable air conditioners. But it is ultimately a short-term adaptation to increasingly dangerous heat rather than a solution to the underlying climate crisis.
For Japan's outdoor workers and event-goers, however, the "human refrigerator" could offer something increasingly valuable during the country's hottest days: a small, mobile refuge from extreme heat.

LONDON, Aug 12 : British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will chair an emergency Cobra meeting on Wednesday to coordinate the government's response to extreme heat, wildfires and worsening drought conditions across the UK. Burnham will meet ministers, officials and emergency...
LONDON, Aug 12 : British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will chair an emergency Cobra meeting on Wednesday to coordinate the government's response to extreme heat, wildfires and worsening drought conditions across the UK.
Burnham will meet ministers, officials and emergency agencies as temperatures continue to climb, with highs of 33 C forecast for Wednesday and up to 38 C expected on Thursday, according to local media reports.
A No 10 spokesperson said the government recognised the challenges posed by the extreme weather, particularly for firefighters, farmers and NHS staff, local media reported.
Wednesday's meeting will be the second Cobra session this year focused on heatwaves, following a meeting in June.
It comes as parts of the UK experience their fifth heatwave of the summer and the number of days with temperatures reaching 30 C or higher has hit a new annual record.
The Met Office said the UK has recorded 35 such days so far this year, surpassing the previous record of 34 days set in 1995. The weather agency has also issued a rare amber extreme heat warning for Thursday.
Green Party leader Zack Polanski called for urgent government action, saying, "We cannot negotiate with the science."
Writing on X, Polanski called for fossil fuel companies to be taxed to help fund firefighting helicopters, alongside measures including a cool space in every community, a maximum working temperature and an end to new oil and gas extraction in the North Sea.
The emergency meeting follows the latest heatwave, which has pushed more parts of England into drought status. Firefighters are also continuing to battle a major wildfire in the New Forest in Hampshire.
On Tuesday, the Met Office said the UK was on course to record its hottest summer on record based on average temperature.
Wales declared a drought on July 30 after sustained high temperatures and deteriorating conditions. A drought had already been declared across large parts of England following record-low rainfall and prolonged heat.
The human impact has also been significant. Last month, the UK Health Security Agency said Britain recorded 2,877 excess deaths during the May and June heatwaves, almost double the 1,504 excess deaths recorded during the summer 2025. (UNI)

full_text:
Nurses are collapsing during shifts amid “inhumane and impossible” conditions caused by extreme heat, their union has warned, as Andy Burnham promised to grapple with “the bigger questions” of climate adaptation.
Amid growing pressure from Labour backbenches to fully acknowledge the urgency of adaptation measures as the climate crisis bites, Burnham said he was for now focusing on the immediate crises caused by an ongoing summer of extreme heat.
Speaking after a meeting of the government’s Cobra emergency committee, Burnham refused to say if the summer had made the case against renewed drilling in the North Sea, which his government is considering.
“It is really important that we deal today with the situation that we are in right now and we focus on making sure that we have the serious incidents under control across the country, and those incidents are under control,” he said.
“The bigger questions obviously will come at the right moment in time,” he added.
An amber warning for heat across large parts of England will come into force again on Thursday morning, with temperatures forecast to reach 36C or potentially higher.
Train passengers on some networks are being warned by rail operators to only travel if the journey is vital, saying services are likely to be disrupted because of the weather.
Three-quarters of England is now officially in drought. Firefighters are continuing to tackle a blaze in the New Forest in Hampshire, with warnings across parts of eastern and southern Scotland about a very high risk of wildfires.
With the number of days of 30C-plus heat in the UK already at a new record of 35, the Royal College of Nursing became the latest union to warn of unsafe working conditions for many members in hospital wards and care homes.
The RCN, which runs an advice hotline, said some staff had collapsed. Others were left dizzy, nauseous or at risk of fainting while dripping with sweat “from head to toe”. They also faced pressure to keep elderly and vulnerable patients safe alongside keeping medications cool.
Working within a critical care unit in an NHS hospital in the south-west of England, a 37-year-old nurse told the Guardian her ward had reached temperatures of more than 30C and staff were struggling in the conditions.
“Our ward doesn’t have air conditioning, and so we’re all really struggling. We’ve had hot summers before, but I can’t remember ever working in conditions like these back to back,” she said.
Another nurse, working in a community health centre in England, said: “It gets to the point you dread going to work, especially when wearing PPE and providing patient care. We drip with sweat from head to toe.”
Prof Nicola Ranger, the general secretary and chief executive of the RCN, said that these testimonies were a “wake-up call”, calling for an urgent programme to install air conditioning, improve ventilation and ensure heat-appropriate uniforms were available.
On Monday, the Fire Brigades Union warned that firefighters needed new equipment and resources to face the growing threats from a climate changing at speed.
According to a freedom of information request submitted by the Guardian, just 20 staff are working on climate adaptation within the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
The government has been warned by the climate change adaptation committee that it is lagging far behind in terms of adapting to a new climate.
Speaking on Wednesday morning, Burnham raised the idea of a possible ban on disposable barbecues, which are a known fire risk. Later in the day, he said retailers should withdraw them from sale, adding: “Longer term we will look at whether a temporary ban in the summer months is justified.”
One Labour MP, Chris Hinchliff, who had previously warned Burnham about the need to prepare the country for a fast-changing climate, called for more immediate action, saying the summer “has to be a real wake-up call for Westminster”.
Some Labour MPs are also privately concerned that he has as yet not shown he understands the urgency of the issue.
“Adaptation has always been the poor relation in government,” one Labour MP said. “Look how much better we are at getting energy projects off the ground than reservoirs.”
Some MPs argued Burnham took too long to hold a Cobra meeting, with one saying: “He barely talks about the climate crisis. He should be doing as many social media video clips on this as he does on the cost of living crisis.”
Hinchliff, the MP for North East Hertfordshire, said the events of the summer should be enough to spark action.
He said: “It’s a well-recognised fact that our country was built for a climate that no longer exists. It’s putting enormous pressure on our infrastructure, our railways, our schools, our hospitals, and it threatens a real impact on people’s living standards. This has to be one of the top priorities for government.
“It is indisputable that up to now we haven’t treated these issues with the importance that they deserve, and the proof is what we are experiencing.”
Another MP said Burnham should use the subject to his advantage and “lean into climate adaptability”.
“Let Nigel Farage be on the side of the wildfires – he can be the pro-wildfire politician, and Andy can be the anti-wildfire prime minister. This is an opportunity for him to seize,” they added.
Health and social care secretary Yvette Cooper said: “The extreme heat is hitting public health and our NHS. Across the NHS and social care, staff are doing a remarkable job to respond to rising A&E attendances and ambulance call-outs, heat problems among the elderly and difficult working conditions. I want to thank them for all their work.
“But I have also been clear that the NHS now needs to plan for summer pressures in the way we currently plan for winter pressures. That includes making sure buildings are more resilient in these new extreme heat conditions as well as responding to additional patient needs.”

Solar boat trip in heatwave not all smooth sailing
Making the most of the ongoing sunny weather, a married couple are attempting to travel 124 miles (200km) down the River Thames - all in a solar powered boat.
Tim Knox's vessel is using only the power of the sun to travel from Lechlade, in Gloucestershire, to Teddington in South West London.
Having set off on Monday, Knox and his wife Sue are now travelling along the river through Oxfordshire, before making it into Berkshire towards the end of the week.
Knox said he had been building solar powered boats for the past 15 years, and that the main reason behind his latest creation was "my wife doesn't like solar [energy]".
"I wanted to build a boat that she really liked going on, because I absolutely adore being on the water - I'm one of the water people," he said.
The couple are taking on the journey as the UK experiences yet another heatwave, which should provide the vessel with plenty of energy for its solar powered battery.
But just days into their expedition, Knox said the weather had also hindered the trip.
"The water shortages are causing a little bit of an issue, which is adding a little bit of a stress to the whole thing - it's become a torture test for the boat, and for me and my wife," he said.
He said timetabled lock opening times, implemented due to low water levels, had left the boat needing to "rush between them".
"The mad thing about the boat is that if you go at a gentle speed, you can easily do it on solar power, but we've had to rush between locks," he said.
"So just like with a car, if you go fast, you use more fuel - which is eking into my battery power."
Knox said the days on the water had been "more gruelling" than he had predicted.
During their voyage, the couple will take in famous towns along the Thames - including Wallingford, Henley and Eton.
The boat - which Knox has named Dayboat 1 - is set to reach Teddington on Sunday, at which point, its captain said he "might be silly enough" to carry on to the tidal Thames in central London.

MPs make fireworks plea in 'tinderbox' conditions
Two MPs and the council leader have urged people to stop setting off "nuisance" fireworks during the heatwave to stop fires taking hold.
In an open letter, Peterborough's Labour MPs Andrew Pakes and Sam Carling, and Labour city council leader Shabina Qayyum asked people to "think twice" due to the "tinder-dry conditions".
They also cited "ongoing noise nuisance caused by anti-social, late-night firework use in recent days" and also advised people against using disposable barbecues.
Pakes said: "Fireworks can be brilliant fun when they're organised and done properly, but right now, in this heat, with everything as dry as it is, a single spark is all it takes to cause real damage."
He added that firefighters were already under significant pressure and said residents could help reduce the risk by avoiding activities that could ignite dry vegetation.
The letter references Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service's continued efforts to tackle a major peatland fire at Holme Fen Nature Reserve, which has occupied crews since Saturday. The cause of the fire is yet to be established.
The BBC has asked the fire service how many firework-related incidents they have attended in recent weeks.
'Exercise caution'
Carling, MP for the North West Cambridgeshire constituency, which includes Holme Fen, said: "This isn't about spoiling anyone's fun; it's about recognising that conditions right now make fireworks and disposable barbecues genuinely dangerous."
Qayyum added: "I'd urge everyone to exercise real caution. That means thinking twice about fireworks and disposable barbecues, and looking out for each other by speaking up if you see something risky."
The Nene Park Trust has banned the use of disposable barbecues in its parks, including at Ferry Meadows in Peterborough.
The fire service is urging residents to use fireworks responsibly, including supervising sparklers carefully, and reminding people that fireworks must not be sold to under-18s or set off in public places.
Cambridgeshire Police said it had received one report in the past week relating to fireworks being let off near homes.
The call was made by a concerned resident in Dogsthorpe in Peterborough at about 22:00 BST on Monday.
On Wednesday, residents of the Longthorpe and Netherton area of the city said fireworks were being let off for periods of several minutes during the daytime.

Centuries-old lost gardens revealed by heatwave
Traces of centuries-old gardens and buildings have been revealed by months of hot, dry weather.
Staff at the Bishop's Palace in Wells, Somerset, said visitors had been "fascinated" to see signs of garden designs from the 18th Century, while relics of old structures at Glastonbury Abbey and Longleat House have also been exposed by the conditions.
The phenomenon occurs when grass laid over old flowerbeds or stone has shorter roots so burns more quickly, creating a contrast with the more bedded-in lawn around it.
James Cross, the head gardener at the Bishop's Palace, said some remnants of gardens past had appeared in spots they had never noticed before.
"They're showing up almost certainly Dutch-style gardens that were popular here, or at least laid out here, probably [in] the middle of the 1700s," he said.
The old garden, he explained, featured gravel pathways and hedging in a formal and "very symmetrical" style, with recent drone footage showing elements that had never been uncovered before.
"It has been fascinating to find those Dutch-style gardens showing up in a spot that we didn't think there was actually anything," he said.
Historical drainage systems have reappeared in Stoke Park in Bristol, too, following months of prolonged heat and dry weather.
Steve England, an outdoor educator, horticulturist and historian, said the lines that stretch across the field date back to medieval times when monks used to farm the land.
"They dug a trench, and they lined it about a foot deep with crushed limestone stones, basically gravel," he said.
"When it rains, all the rain is going to go into the little trenches and be filtered off somewhere, so it was drying up the land."
According to England, the lines had become visible because the stones underneath had heated up and killed the grass roots.
"This is what makes Stoke Park one of the more special places in Bristol - it's the fact that there's layer upon layer upon layer of history," he added.
Lucy Newman, the collections manager at Glastonbury Abbey, told the BBC the parched conditions had uncovered traces of foundations, stone columns and earlier excavation work.
"This year in particular, they've been really sharp and really clear," she said.
"So it helps our visitors get an understanding of which bits of the Abbey [remain]... we've got a few bits and pieces where we've still got tall walls, but not very many, [so] it just gives that little bit of extra information on the ground."
At Longleat a 'leat' - a West Country term for a man-made stream feeding a watermill - has been revealed, as well as the possible location of the watermill itself. The leat is thought to have given the historic estate its name.
Drone footage has also revealed "the clearest evidence in memory" of long-lost formal gardens, Longleat curator Dr James Ford said, including previously unrecorded features dating back to the 17th Century.
"Altogether, these marks offer a rare glimpse of earlier phases of Longleat's landscape, from its medieval priory origins to its later formal gardens and 18th-century redesign," said Ford.

Commentary: Japan’s earthquake shows extreme heat can turn one disaster into two
As the climate changes, the impact of any disaster will increasingly depend not only on the primary event but also on the climatic conditions in which it unfolds, says a climatology professor.
DURHAM, England: Emergency workers attempting to rescue survivors after a recent earthquake in Kyushu, Japan, also had to cope with extreme summer heat.
After the earthquake killed at least 38 people and left thousands homeless in late July, daytime temperatures climbed into the high 30 degrees and in some places hit 40°C for the first time ever, with high humidity.
Extreme heat affects almost every aspect of an emergency response. For the close to 7,000 people in 130 evacuation shelters and in temporary accommodation across the Kumamoto region, on the southernmost of Japan’s four main islands, hot and humid conditions increase the risk of dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke.
Older adults, infants and people with chronic illnesses are particularly susceptible. It is suspected that one older woman has already died of heatstroke while sheltering in her car.
Heat also makes it harder for people to sleep, especially when air conditioning is unavailable or electricity supplies have been interrupted. Poor sleep can worsen stress, impair decision-making and slow recovery following traumatic events. Emergency responders are similarly affected.
Rescue work, debris removal and infrastructure repairs are physically demanding activities. High temperatures reduce physical performance, increase fatigue and require more frequent rest breaks, potentially slowing recovery operations.
The effects extend beyond health. Damaged water infrastructure increases demand for drinking water precisely when supplies may be constrained. Electricity demand for cooling rises at the same time as power outages. Some medicines require refrigeration. Businesses face longer interruptions. Schools and community facilities may remain closed for longer. This creates a complex web of interacting risks.
Water supplies have been disrupted in some areas and electricity outages have limited access to cooling equipment, leaving evacuation centres very hot. These conditions create a second emergency that receives far less attention than the earthquake itself but can have profound consequences for public health and recovery. This is an example of what hazard scientists call a compound event.
THE SECOND EMERGENCY
Often natural hazards are thought of as isolated events, but they frequently interact with one another, so that their combined impacts are greater than the sum of each individually. Sometimes the interaction is between different weather extremes, such as heatwaves followed by drought or wildfire. In other cases, climate hazards combine with other geophysical hazards such as earthquakes.
The conditions in 2026 are very different to those when Kumamoto last experienced large earthquakes, in April 2016.
The 2016 Kumamoto earthquake caused widespread destruction. However, the April temperatures were relatively mild. The recent earthquake occurred during one of the hottest parts of the Japanese summer. Although rescue priorities remain the same, the environmental conditions are fundamentally different.
As the climate changes, the impact of any disaster will increasingly depend not only on the primary event but also on the climatic conditions in which it unfolds. The Kumamoto earthquake shows how extreme heat can become a powerful disaster risk multiplier. A similar lesson emerged after the catastrophic western Japan floods of 2018, when a record-breaking heatwave, subsequently shown by research to have been virtually impossible without human-induced climate change, compounded the disaster, increasing health risks and hampering recovery efforts.
Together, these events demonstrate how heatwaves following other disasters can amplify the consequences.
PLANNING AHEAD
The Kumamoto earthquake shows that disaster resilience is no longer just about building stronger infrastructure or improving earthquake-resistant design. It also means preparing communities for multiple interacting hazards.
As climate change increases the frequency and intensity of extreme heat, those planning for emergencies will have to factor this in.
The question is no longer simply how societies respond to earthquakes or heatwaves separately, but how they prepare for all of these circumstances.
As the world experiences more heatwaves, extreme temperatures will pose new challenges for disaster recovery during the hottest parts of the year.
Glenn McGregor is Professor of Climatology at Durham University. This commentary first appeared on The Conversation.

Representational image
Doha, Qatar: As summer temperatures soar in Qatar, children can move from playing outdoors to becoming seriously unwell in a matter of minutes, with dehydration, heat exhaustion and heat stroke among the risks parents need to recognise early, according to Chair of Pediatric Medicine at Sidra Medicine, Dr. Ahmed Al Hammadi.
Children are particularly vulnerable to extreme heat because their bodies generate more heat during physical activity and are less efficient than adults at regulating body temperature. Infants and young children face an even greater risk because they depend on adults to ensure they remain hydrated, appropriately dressed and protected from prolonged heat exposure.
“The most common conditions we see include dehydration, heat cramps, heat exhaustion, and, in more severe cases, heat stroke,” Dr Al Hammadi told The Peninsula.
While most heat-related illnesses are preventable, he stressed that parents should not wait for children to complain of thirst before offering fluids. “The habit worth building is steady drinking throughout the day rather than waiting for thirst, because by the time a child feels thirsty, dehydration has already begun,” he said.
Early signs of dehydration include thirst, dry lips and mouth, reduced and darker urine, and low energy. In babies, parents may notice fewer wet nappies, while young children may become irritable or suddenly lose interest in eating and drinking. As dehydration worsens, children can develop lethargy, sunken eyes, few or no tears when crying and difficulty being roused.
One of the most important distinctions for parents is knowing the difference between heat exhaustion and potentially life-threatening heat stroke.
A child experiencing heat exhaustion will typically remain responsive but may be very thirsty, tired, dizzy or nauseated, with heavy sweating and cool, clammy skin.
Heat stroke is much more serious and occurs when the body loses its ability to regulate its temperature. Warning signs include confusion, unusual drowsiness, seizures or loss of consciousness. The child may stop sweating and develop hot, dry skin.
“My guidance is simple: if a child is confused or not behaving like themselves after time in the heat, treat it as an emergency immediately,” Dr Al Hammadi said.
Parents should seek medical attention if a child is unable to keep fluids down because of persistent vomiting, shows signs of moderate to severe dehydration, develops a persistent fever following heat exposure, or fails to improve after being moved to a cool environment and given fluids.
Emergency medical care is required without delay if a child becomes faint or extremely tired, is unusually sleepy or difficult to wake, becomes confused or loses coordination, develops a severe headache, breathes faster or deeper than normal, has a seizure or loses consciousness.
“At Sidra Medicine, we encourage parents to trust their instincts,” Dr Al Hammadi said. “If a child looks seriously unwell or is deteriorating despite home measures, it is always safer to seek help.”
Heat is not the only summer danger. Swimming pools, beaches and other bodies of water can present serious risks, particularly when children are not under direct adult supervision.
“A young child should never be alone in or near water even for a few seconds, and whether they can swim makes little difference to that rule,” Dr Al Hammadi said, stressing that drowning can happen silently and quickly.
He advised parents to ensure children swim only in designated areas with appropriate supervision. Properly fitted life jackets should be used when children are boating or taking part in water sports, while age-appropriate swimming lessons can form part of a broader approach to water safety. Inflatable toys, armbands and other flotation devices should never be treated as replacements for a life jacket or direct adult supervision.
Sun protection is another essential part of summer safety. For infants under six months, Dr Al Hammadi recommends relying on shade, protective clothing and hats rather than routine sunscreen use.
For children aged six months and older, he recommends a broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher on exposed skin. Mineral-based formulations containing zinc oxide or titanium dioxide may be particularly suitable for children with sensitive skin.
Sunscreen should be applied 15 to 30 minutes before going outdoors and reapplied every two hours, as well as after swimming or heavy sweating.
However, sunscreen should complement rather than replace other protective measures such as shade and appropriate clothing.
“Hydration is not optional; sunscreen is not cosmetic, and supervision around water is not negotiable,” Dr Al Hammadi said.
He urged families to make fluids, shade, protective clothing and sunscreen part of their daily summer routine, while learning to recognise the early signs of dehydration, heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
“These are not small details; they are life-saving habits,” he said. “By practising them consistently, we can ensure that summer remains a season of play and growth, not of preventable tragedy.”

The weather agency issued a red warning for Odisha, forecasting very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across several parts of the state.
The national weather agency in its morning message said, "The well-marked low-pressure area over North Bay of Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh-West Bengal coast moved northwestwards. It is likely to continue to move northwestwards across Gangetic West Bengal towards Jharkhand and may concentrate into a depression during the next 12 hours."
A depression is a weather system that is stronger than a low-pressure area but less intense than a tropical cyclone.
While issuing a red warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Odisha on Thursday, the IMD said Gangetic West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand were also likely to be affected by the ongoing wet spell triggered by the low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal.
In view of the weather conditions, the IMD advised fishermen not to venture into the North Bay of Bengal and along the Odisha-West Bengal-Bangladesh coast until August 14.
According to the Meteorological Centre, Bhubaneswar, Bhograi in Balasore district recorded the highest rainfall of 236 mm, followed by 230 mm at Shyamakhuntam, 215 mm at Baripada in Mayurbhanj district and 204 mm at Rajghat in Balasore district.
According to news agency PTI, Balasore town recorded 137 mm of rainfall by 5.30 am on Thursday, the highest in the state during the period.
Reports of very heavy rainfall were also received from the Similipal Hills in Mayurbhanj district.
The heavy rains in Mayurbhanj have led to a rise in the water levels of the Budhabalanga and Jalaka rivers in Balasore district. A large part of Balasore town is also experiencing waterlogging, an official said.
Meanwhile, in the wake of the heavy rainfall since last night, the authorities declared the closure of all educational institutions in Mayurbhanj district on Thursday.
A district administration notification directed all headmasters, headmistresses, principals and teachers to report to their respective schools as usual and inform students and their parents or guardians about the closure through available communication channels, including class WhatsApp groups, phone calls and SMS.

Colombia President Abelardo De La Espriella declared an economic emergency following the devastating earthquake and announced relief measures for affected families.
The government will provide utility payment relief, rental subsidies, tax and financial assistance, while a new Milagro Fund will support reconstruction.
International aid and rescue teams are arriving as the death toll rises and search-and-rescue operations continue across affected areas.
Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella declared an economic emergency on Thursday following the devastating earthquake that killed hundreds and left thousands missing, announcing a series of relief and reconstruction measures for affected communities.
However, according to CNN, Colombia began receiving international aid and rescuers after initially refusing some offers in the crucial hours following Monday’s devastating earthquake. As per Reuters, the death toll has now risen to 265.
What Relief Measures Has Colombia Announced?
Espriella announced the economic emergency to take measures that would assist the affected families. “We will implement temporary reliefs on public utility payments, rental subsidies for those who lost their homes, tax and financial reliefs, economic support for the most vulnerable families, and backup mechanisms for affected merchants and small business owners,” he said.
He also announced about the creation of Milagro Fund, which will channel national and international resources for the reconstruction of hospitals, educational centers, housing, roads, airports, and other affected infrastructure.
The government announced they will adopt measures to reactivate the economy, stimulate investment, and generate employment in the hardest-hit territories.
Why Did Colombia Declare An Economic Emergency?
After the 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck the nation, at least 250 people were reported dead, and many more injured. Espriella's broader message said his priority is to reduce the burden on affected people, rebuild damaged infrastructure and restore normalcy.
Leaders across the Americas had offered support immediately after the earthquake struck. But Colombia either turned some of them down or limited how they would help, as per CNN. This came withing the critical window of 72 hours for rescuing survivors trapped underneath buildings. Several countries and organisations said they had not received a request for aid from Colombian authorities.
Spokesperson for the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, Jens Laerke, told CNN, “If that happens, the United Nations system and humanitarian actors are prepared to provide all the support we can.”
Meanwhile, the Trump Administration has mobilized an immediate response following the devastating earthquake. The Department of State announced $15.5 million in life-saving emergency shelter, food, and protection assistance, in addition to post-earthquake structural assessments.
The Department also activated a Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART), which includes humanitarian experts from across the State Department.
Locals and officials in Colombia have begun a massive search and rescue effort to find survivors. The United States Geological Survey said the magnitude 7.4 earthquake occurred primarily due to strike-slip faulting at a depth of approximately 110 kilometres.
In simple terms, a strike-slip earthquake occurs when two blocks of Earth’s crust slide horizontally past one another, rather than moving up or down.
